## HDT-O Discussion

### Our understanding of HDT-O and its mapping to Wikibase and Betwixt

We understand a Heritage Digital Twin (`HC2`) as an evolving, structured body of knowledge about a heritage object. In our implementation, Wikibase provides the operational environment for maintaining this knowledge. Each Wikibase item serves as the entry point to a digital twin, with statements describing the object and relationships connecting it to other digital twins.

The [Dēliņi farmhouse (Q7328)](https://reprexbase.eu/fu/Item:Q7328) is part of the [Dēliņi farmstead (Q5582)](https://reprexbase.eu/fu/Item:Q5582). Two historical photographs, [frontal view with well (Q7362)](https://reprexbase.eu/fu/Item:Q7362) and [oblique view (Q7363)](https://reprexbase.eu/fu/Item:Q7363), depict the farmhouse. Each photograph may have its own digital twin (`HC2`), while its digital image may also serve as a digital representation (`HC5`) of the farmhouse.

We use [Betwixt review tables](https://usebetwixt.com/examples/EADH2026/EADH_workshop_exercise_04.html) as an intermediate representation for producing and reviewing knowledge, as we have presented this in the _European Association of Digital Humanities 2026_ conference paper and methodology workshop. Curators examine proposed claims, supporting evidence and existing statements, and record their decisions. Accepted propositions form a Heritage Proposition Set (`HC16`), which can be incorporated into the relevant digital twin. For example, the farmhouse may be classified as a [building (Q3867)](https://reprexbase.eu/fu/Item:Q3867) (`P14`) and associated with the heritage of the [Livonians (Q46)](https://reprexbase.eu/fu/Item:Q46) (`P480`).

We propose maintaining separate, chronologically organised collections of Betwixt reviews for each digital twin. Individual review documents preserve the evidence, authorship, decisions and provenance of the review process. Using PROV-O, we link these records to the resulting proposition sets and published Wikibase statements.

Our central modelling assumption is that **the digital twin evolves, while individual reviewed proposition sets and finalised review records remain persistent and independently identifiable**. This allows curators to access current accepted knowledge without losing the history of how that knowledge was established.

The pseudo-Turtle below illustrates our proposed mapping between Wikibase, HDT-O and PROV-O. It is intended as a conceptual example rather than a complete ontology implementation.

```         

@prefix wd:   <https://reprexbase.eu/fu/entity/> .
@prefix wdt:  <https://reprexbase.eu/fu/prop/direct/> .
@prefix hdt:  <https://example.org/hdto/> .
@prefix prov: <http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#> .
@prefix dct:  <http://purl.org/dc/terms/> .
@prefix ex:   <https://example.org/delini/> .
@prefix xsd:  <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .

# ===================================================
# 1. HERITAGE DIGITAL TWINS (HC2)
# ===================================================

wd:Q7328
    a hdt:HC2 ;
    dct:title "Dēliņi farmhouse (BDM 8068)"@en ;
    wdt:P14 wd:Q3867 ;          # instance of: building
    wdt:P16 wd:Q5582 ;          # part of: farmstead
    wdt:P480 wd:Q46 ;           # heritage of: Livonians
    wdt:P165 wd:Q7362, wd:Q7363 ;
    hdt:HP33 ex:house-propositions-1 ;
    prov:wasDerivedFrom wd:Q9328 .

wd:Q5582
    a hdt:HC2 ;
    dct:title "Dēliņi farmstead"@en ;
    wdt:P14 wd:Q7370 ;          # instance of: farmstead
    wdt:P480 wd:Q46 ;           # heritage of: Livonians
    hdt:HP33 ex:farmstead-propositions-1 ;
    prov:wasDerivedFrom wd:Q9582 .

# ===================================================
# 2. PHOTOGRAPHS AS DIGITAL TWINS (HC2) or HC5
# ===================================================

wd:Q7362
    a hdt:HC2 ;
    dct:title
      "Dēliņi farmhouse, frontal view with well (photo)"@en .

wd:Q7363
    a hdt:HC2 ;
    dct:title
      "Dēliņi farmhouse, oblique view (photo)"@en .

# ===================================================
# 3. BETWIXT REVIEW COLLECTIONS
# ===================================================

wd:Q9328
    a prov:Collection ;
    dct:title "Betwixt reviews of Q7328"@en ;
    ex:reviewsTwin wd:Q7328 ;
    prov:hadMember
        ex:house-review-1,
        ex:house-review-2 .

wd:Q9582
    a prov:Collection ;
    dct:title "Betwixt reviews of Q5582"@en ;
    ex:reviewsTwin wd:Q5582 ;
    prov:hadMember ex:farmstead-review-1 .

# ===================================================
# 4. PERSISTENT BETWIXT REVIEW DOCUMENTS (HC15)
# ===================================================

ex:house-review-1
    a hdt:HC15, prov:Entity ;
    dct:identifier
      "review-Q7328_final-1.html" ;
    dct:creator ex:reviewer-A ;
    dct:issued "2026-09-01"^^xsd:date .

ex:house-review-2
    a hdt:HC15, prov:Entity ;
    dct:identifier
      "review-Q7328_final-2.html" ;
    dct:creator ex:reviewer-B ;
    dct:issued "2026-10-01"^^xsd:date ;
    prov:wasRevisionOf ex:house-review-1 .

ex:farmstead-review-1
    a hdt:HC15, prov:Entity ;
    dct:identifier
      "review-Q5582_final-1.html" ;
    dct:creator ex:reviewer-A ;
    dct:issued "2026-09-01"^^xsd:date .

# ===================================================
# 5. WARRANTED PROPOSITION SETS (HC16)
# ===================================================

ex:house-propositions-1
    a hdt:HC16 ;
    prov:wasDerivedFrom ex:house-review-1 .

ex:farmstead-propositions-1
    a hdt:HC16 ;
    prov:wasDerivedFrom ex:farmstead-review-1 .

# Contents of house-propositions-1:
#   wd:Q7328 wdt:P14  wd:Q3867 .
#   wd:Q7328 wdt:P480 wd:Q46 .

# Contents of farmstead-propositions-1:
#   wd:Q5582 wdt:P14  wd:Q7370 .
#   wd:Q5582 wdt:P480 wd:Q46 .
```


## Questions for the HDT-O authors

### Our proposed implementation

We envisage publishing and maintaining our Heritage Digital Twins (`HC2`) in Wikibase. Wikibase will serve as our operational knowledge base, where accepted propositions are published as statements, linked to other heritage resources and supported by references to their provenance.



We understand that the ECHOES team would like to incorporate our digital twins into its own infrastructure. We therefore envisage developing a tool that projects our Wikibase knowledge graphs into the ontologies and RDF structures preferred by ECHOES, including HDT-O and its dependencies. We would appreciate guidance on the expected exchange format and, ideally, a reference **SHACL validation suite and EARL test cases or reporting requirements**. These would allow us to develop and test the projection systematically, demonstrate conformance and identify interoperability problems before exchanging data.

The following questions concern the conceptual mapping and interoperability requirements rather than the internal implementation of our Wikibase and Betwixt systems.

## Questions about modelling, publication and interoperability

1. **Photographs as digital twins or digital representations (`HC2` vs `HC5`).** Is there a preference for modelling historical photographs as `HC2` rather than merely `HC5`? A photograph can itself have an evolving body of knowledge, including attribution, dating, identification, provenance and permissions of use. Can the same photograph have its own digital twin while also serving as a digital representation of another heritage object?

2. **Archival records, library resources and ontology interoperability.** Our heritage resources include archival records and collections that are more naturally described using [Records in Contexts](https://www.ica.org/ica-network/expert-groups/egad/records-in-contexts-ric/) (RiC-O) than CIDOC CRM, with RiC being itself very much CIDOC-influenced, but far more appropriate for documents than CIDOC. Can RiC-O entities be mapped into HDT-O without losing their archival semantics? Similarly, can library resources described using DCTERMS participate in the same digital twin framework? Do you envisage recommended mappings or interoperability patterns for these ontologies?

3. **Wikibase items as operational digital twins (`HC2`).** We propose treating existing Wikibase items as operational `HC2` instances, rather than creating separate items for the digital twins. Each item maintains an evolving set of accepted statements and links to related resources. Is this an acceptable approach for an HDT-O projection?

4. **Reviewed proposition sets (`HC16`) and Wikibase statements.** Betwixt produces reviewed proposition sets (`HC16`), whose accepted claims are published as ordinary Wikibase statements. The review datasets preserve the evidence, decisions and provenance supporting these statements. We propose this as our knowledge production and publication workflow.

5. **Current and former proposition sets (`HP33` and `HP34`).** HDT-O distinguishes proposition sets currently contained in a digital twin (`HP33`) from those previously contained (`HP34`). In our approach, accepted Betwixt propositions enter Wikibase, while subsequent reviews may revise or withdraw them. Does `HP34` apply only to propositions that were previously accepted and later superseded, or can it also describe propositions that were considered during review but never accepted into the digital twin?

6. **HDT-O and PROV-O interoperability.** We use PROV-O to describe how reviewed proposition sets (`HC16`) are derived from persistent Betwixt review documents (`HC15`), including cases where multiple reviews contribute to the same proposition set. Does HDT-O envisage a more specific relationship for this purpose, or is PROV-O sufficient?

7. **Digital twin composition (`HP3`).** We distinguish physical part–whole relationships from the composition of digital twins. Is `HP3` intended to express an independently established digital composition, rather than automatically following physical part–whole relationships? If one digital twin is a component of another, does this imply any inclusion or inheritance of its `HC16` proposition sets? This is particularly important for archival records, which may belong to different Record Sets, potentially with overlapping or changing arrangements.

8. **Digital twin snapshots (`HP28`) and persistence.** Our Wikibase digital twins evolve as reviewed propositions are added, revised or withdrawn. We preserve the Betwixt reviews and their provenance, while Wikibase maintains its own revision history. Does HDT-O envisage complete, persistent snapshots (`HP28`) as an essential part of digital twin maintenance, or are they optional? For exchanging digital twins between institutions, is there a recommended way to package their current propositions, historical reviews and provenance?

### Validation and interoperability

We do not envisage replacing Wikibase with an ECHOES-specific repository. Instead, we propose developing a reproducible RDF projection from our operational Wikibase and Betwixt environment into the ontology structures expected by ECHOES. To implement and validate this projection, we would appreciate the following:
To implement the mapping reliably, we would particularly appreciate:

- A reference set of SHACL shapes defining the expected structure and constraints of HDT-O-compatible RDF.
- Representative positive and negative test cases, with expected validation outcomes.
- Guidance on EARL reporting so that we can document which interoperability and conformance tests our projection tool passes or fails.
- An example of a complete, valid Heritage Digital Twin exchange package, including proposition sets, digital representations and provenance.
